# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secuura/Blockchain s150 (`%171`, 2026-09-08 14:32→15:08 — #907 amend+merge, #793 merge, Peter's fourteen PRs) | **Caught Wednesday twice in six minutes and was right both times, and the catches came from REORDERING the brief rather than obeying it.** Told to work Peter's list, it ran the measurement pass FIRST — stated reason: *"everything else depended on not acting on stale state"* — and that is the only reason two Wednesday errors cost nothing. (1) Wednesday said Kam's two #793 rulings were undelivered and told KAM nobody had executed them; s150 measured `audit-baseline.json` at the head and proved all five clauses present, 35 rows vs develop's 31, delta exactly +4, zero develop rows lost, plus the re-triage ticket already filed as KS-997 — then added the sharper diagnosis Wednesday had missed: `history.md` said done too, so **two independent records said done and one column said undelivered, and the column won.** (2) Wednesday handed it a heuristic — *"a DIRTY mark is assertive and probably real"* — and it measured all nine: **all three DIRTY marks were wrong.** Its replacement was adopted verbatim. **On #721 it refused the disposal it was offered**, proving the PR was a `CLAUDE.md` docs fix retiring the live *"CLEAN = green"* instruction rather than KS-660's implementation — the very sentence that caused the day's episode. Then, told to prove the replacement text CORRECT and not merely different, **it found the replacement itself stale** (#718's worked example no longer behaves as described) and did not merge. It established Peter's eight-day wait was on NOBODY — his preferred landing was implemented on 1 and 7 Sep and never written on the PR — and posted the answer with his requested evidence. On #895/#896 it refused to rebase (rewriting another author's head) and merged additively instead, proving #896's develop side was purely the formatter by running prettier on the merge-base and comparing byte-wise, with a control that the merge-base was not already formatted. **It also retracted its own earlier "both are dirty" claim unprompted.** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Two merges (`27b0ee294`, `9806be0ac`), KS-997/999/1000 filed, KS-365 down to one upstream condition. Zero holds crossed, nobody messaged outside a PR/ticket comment. **The two errors scored here are WEDNESDAY'S, not s150's** — recorded in `_ledger.md`. |
| QA agent (fleet, Secuura KS-989 / PR #906 @ `9f9a2a788` — TIER 2 through-code, 2026-09-08 13:45→13:59) | **The strongest gate this fleet has run, and it took fourteen minutes.** It re-derived the load-bearing claim from `--shared` clones at each SHA — and when the control SHA came back green it PLANTED A VIOLATION there rather than trusting the green, then restored it byte-identical. It found the control SHA was the merge's own first parent, which is the strongest control the claim admits. It re-ran the builder's red-proof AND added SEVEN independent tampers with TWO inert controls, proving the driver does not red on any edit. It proved the new suite BLOCKS the runner rather than merely appearing in its glob. It converted Wednesday's *"a stated gap is not automatically an acceptable one"* into F1, a MAJOR, by measuring the gap itself against the real tree. Nine items under NOT TESTED, including four it could have quietly omitted. | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | GO-WITH-FINDINGS, 4 findings, 2 MAJOR — neither a regression. # Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.

> ## ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 ~08:1x — Kam SENT the re-issue same hour ("email sent").
